content.latin: Veníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
content.english: Come let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.

content.latin: Ant. Regem ventúrum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. The Lord, the King who is to come * O come, let us adore Him.

content.latin: Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
content.english: For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.

content.latin: Ant. Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. O come, let us adore Him.

content.latin: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius (genuflectitur) veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
content.english: For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. (genuflect) Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.

content.latin: Ant. Regem ventúrum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. The Lord, the King who is to come * O come, let us adore Him.

content.latin: Hódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
content.english: Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.

content.latin: Ant. Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. O come, let us adore Him.

content.latin: Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
content.english: Forty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.

content.latin: Vocábit ad cælum pios;

content.latin: Psalmus 1 [1]
content.english: Psalm 1 [1]

content.latin: 1:1 Beátus vir, qui non ábiit in consílio impiórum, et in via peccatórum non stetit, * et in cáthedra pestiléntiæ non sedit:
content.english: 1:1 Blessed is the man who hath not walked in the counsel of the ungodly, nor stood in the way of sinners, * nor sat in the chair of pestilence.

content.latin: 1:2 Sed in lege Dómini volúntas eius, * et in lege eius meditábitur die ac nocte.
content.english: 1:2 But his will is in the law of the Lord, * and on his law he shall meditate day and night.

content.latin: 1:3 Et erit tamquam lignum, quod plantátum est secus decúrsus aquárum, * quod fructum suum dabit in témpore suo:
content.english: 1:3 And he shall be like a tree which is planted near the running waters, * which shall bring forth its fruit, in due season.

content.latin: 1:3 Et fólium eius non défluet: * et ómnia quæcúmque fáciet, prosperabúntur.
content.english: 1:3 And his leaf shall not fall off: * and all whatsoever he shall do shall prosper.

content.latin: 1:4 Non sic ímpii, non sic: * sed tamquam pulvis, quem próicit ventus a fácie terræ.
content.english: 1:4 Not so the wicked, not so: * but like the dust, which the wind driveth from the face of the earth.

content.latin: 1:5 Ídeo non resúrgent ímpii in iudício: * neque peccatóres in concílio iustórum.
content.english: 1:5 Therefore the wicked shall not rise again in judgment: * nor sinners in the council of the just.

content.latin: 1:6 Quóniam novit Dóminus viam iustórum: * et iter impiórum períbit.
content.english: 1:6 For the Lord knoweth the way of the just: * and the way of the wicked shall perish.

content.latin: Psalmus 2 [2]
content.english: Psalm 2 [2]

content.latin: 2:1 Quare fremuérunt gentes: * et pópuli meditáti sunt inánia?
content.english: 2:1 Why have the Gentiles raged, * and the people devised vain things?

content.latin: 2:2 Astitérunt reges terræ, et príncipes convenérunt in unum * advérsus Dóminum, et advérsus Christum eius.
content.english: 2:2 The kings of the earth stood up, and the princes met together, * against the Lord and against his Christ.

content.latin: 2:3 Dirumpámus víncula eórum: * et proiciámus a nobis iugum ipsórum.
content.english: 2:3 Let us break their bonds asunder: * and let us cast away their yoke from us.

content.latin: 2:4 Qui hábitat in cælis, irridébit eos: * et Dóminus subsannábit eos.
content.english: 2:4 He that dwelleth in heaven shall laugh at them: * and the Lord shall deride them.

content.latin: 2:5 Tunc loquétur ad eos in ira sua, * et in furóre suo conturbábit eos.
content.english: 2:5 Then shall he speak to them in his anger, * and trouble them in his rage.

content.latin: 2:6 Ego autem constitútus sum Rex ab eo super Sion montem sanctum eius, * prǽdicans præcéptum eius.
content.english: 2:6 But I am appointed king by him over Sion his holy mountain, * preaching his commandment.

content.latin: 2:7 Dóminus dixit ad me: * Fílius meus es tu, ego hódie génui te.
content.english: 2:7 The Lord hath said to me: * Thou art my son, this day have I begotten thee.

content.latin: 2:8 Póstula a me, et dabo tibi gentes hereditátem tuam, * et possessiónem tuam términos terræ.
content.english: 2:8 Ask of me, and I will give thee the Gentiles for thy inheritance, * and the utmost parts of the earth for thy possession.

content.latin: 2:9 Reges eos in virga férrea, * et tamquam vas fíguli confrínges eos.
content.english: 2:9 Thou shalt rule them with a rod of iron, * and shalt break them in pieces like a potter’s vessel.

content.latin: 2:10 Et nunc, reges, intellégite: * erudímini, qui iudicátis terram.
content.english: 2:10 And now, O ye kings, understand: * receive instruction, you that judge the earth.

content.latin: 2:11 Servíte Dómino in timóre: * et exsultáte ei cum tremóre.
content.english: 2:11 Serve ye the Lord with fear: * and rejoice unto him with trembling.

content.latin: 2:12 Apprehéndite disciplínam, nequándo irascátur Dóminus, * et pereátis de via iusta.
content.english: 2:12 Embrace discipline, lest at any time the Lord be angry, * and you perish from the just way.

content.latin: 2:13 Cum exárserit in brevi ira eius: * beáti omnes qui confídunt in eo.
content.english: 2:13 When his wrath shall be kindled in a short time, * blessed are all they that trust in him.

content.latin: Psalmus 3 [3]
content.english: Psalm 3 [3]

content.latin: 3:2 Dómine, quid multiplicáti sunt qui tríbulant me? * multi insúrgunt advérsum me.
content.english: 3:2 Why, O Lord, are they multiplied that afflict me? * many are they who rise up against me.

content.latin: 3:3 Multi dicunt ánimæ meæ: * Non est salus ipsi in Deo eius.
content.english: 3:3 Many say to my soul: * There is no salvation for him in his God.

content.latin: 3:4 Tu autem, Dómine, suscéptor meus es, * glória mea, et exáltans caput meum.
content.english: 3:4 But thou, O Lord art my protector, * my glory, and the lifter up of my head.

content.latin: 3:5 Voce mea ad Dóminum clamávi: * et exaudívit me de monte sancto suo.
content.english: 3:5 I have cried to the Lord with my voice: * and he hath heard me from his holy hill.

content.latin: 3:6 Ego dormívi, et soporátus sum: * et exsurréxi, quia Dóminus suscépit me.
content.english: 3:6 I have slept and taken my rest: * and I have risen up, because the Lord hath protected me.

content.latin: 3:7 Non timébo míllia pópuli circumdántis me: * exsúrge, Dómine, salvum me fac, Deus meus.
content.english: 3:7 I will not fear thousands of the people, surrounding me: * arise, O Lord; save me, O my God.

content.latin: 3:8 Quóniam tu percussísti omnes adversántes mihi sine causa: * dentes peccatórum contrivísti.
content.english: 3:8 For thou hast struck all them who are my adversaries without cause: * thou hast broken the teeth of sinners.

content.latin: 3:9 Dómini est salus: * et super pópulum tuum benedíctio tua.
content.english: 3:9 Salvation is of the Lord: * and thy blessing is upon thy people.

content.latin: Psalmus 8 [4]
content.english: Psalm 8 [4]

content.latin: 8:2 Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra!
content.english: 8:2 O Lord our Lord, * how admirable is thy name in the whole earth!

content.latin: 8:2 Quóniam eleváta est magnificéntia tua, * super cælos.
content.english: 8:2 For thy magnificence is elevated * above the heavens.

content.latin: 8:3 Ex ore infántium et lacténtium perfecísti laudem propter inimícos tuos, * ut déstruas inimícum et ultórem.
content.english: 8:3 Out of the mouth of infants and of sucklings thou hast perfected praise, because of thy enemies, * that thou mayst destroy the enemy and the avenger.

content.latin: 8:4 Quóniam vidébo cælos tuos, ópera digitórum tuórum: * lunam et stellas, quæ tu fundásti.
content.english: 8:4 For I will behold thy heavens, the works of thy fingers: * the moon and the stars which thou hast founded.

content.latin: 8:5 Quid est homo quod memor es eius? * aut fílius hóminis, quóniam vísitas eum?
content.english: 8:5 What is man that thou art mindful of him? * or the son of man that thou visitest him?

content.latin: 8:6 Minuísti eum paulo minus ab Ángelis, glória et honóre coronásti eum: * et constituísti eum super ópera mánuum tuárum.
content.english: 8:6 Thou hast made him a little less than the angels, thou hast crowned him with glory and honour: * and hast set him over the works of thy hands.

content.latin: 8:8 Ómnia subiecísti sub pédibus eius, * oves et boves univérsas: ínsuper et pécora campi.
content.english: 8:8 Thou hast subjected all things under his feet, * all sheep and oxen: moreover the beasts also of the fields.

content.latin: 8:9 Vólucres cæli, et pisces maris, * qui perámbulant sémitas maris.
content.english: 8:9 The birds of the air, and the fishes of the sea, * that pass through the paths of the sea.

content.latin: 8:10 Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra!
content.english: 8:10 O Lord our Lord, * how admirable is thy name in all the earth!

content.latin: Psalmus 9(2-11) [5]
9:2 Confitébor tibi, Dómine, in toto corde meo: * narrábo ómnia mirabília tua.
content.english: 9:2 I will give praise to thee, O Lord, with my whole heart: * I will relate all thy wonders.

content.latin: 9:3 Lætábor et exsultábo in te: * psallam nómini tuo, Altíssime.
content.english: 9:3 I will be glad and rejoice in thee: * I will sing to thy name, O thou most high.

content.latin: 9:4 In converténdo inimícum meum retrórsum: * infirmabúntur, et períbunt a fácie tua.
content.english: 9:4 When my enemy shall be turned back: * they shall be weakened and perish before thy face.

content.latin: 9:5 Quóniam fecísti iudícium meum et causam meam: * sedísti super thronum, qui iúdicas iustítiam.
content.english: 9:5 For thou hast maintained my judgment and my cause: * thou hast sat on the throne, who judgest justice.

content.latin: 9:6 Increpásti gentes, et périit ímpius: * nomen eórum delésti in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: 9:6 Thou hast rebuked the Gentiles, and the wicked one hath perished: * thou hast blotted out their name for ever and ever.

content.latin: 9:7 Inimíci defecérunt frámeæ in finem: * et civitátes eórum destruxísti.
content.english: 9:7 The swords of the enemy have failed unto the end: * and their cities thou hast destroyed.

content.latin: 9:7 Périit memória eórum cum sónitu: * et Dóminus in ætérnum pérmanet.
content.english: 9:7 Their memory hath perished with a noise. * But the Lord remaineth for ever.

content.latin: 9:8 Parávit in iudício thronum suum: * et ipse iudicábit orbem terræ in æquitáte, iudicábit pópulos in iustítia.
content.english: 9:8 He hath prepared his throne in judgment: * And he shall judge the world in equity, he shall judge the people in justice.

content.latin: 9:10 Et factus est Dóminus refúgium páuperi: * adiútor in opportunitátibus, in tribulatióne.
content.english: 9:10 And the Lord is become a refuge for the poor: * a helper in due time in tribulation.

content.latin: 9:11 Et sperent in te qui novérunt nomen tuum: * quóniam non dereliquísti quæréntes te, Dómine.
content.english: 9:11 And let them trust in thee who know thy name: * for thou hast not forsaken them that seek thee, O Lord.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Rex noster advéniet Christus, quem Ioánnes prædicávit Agnum esse ventúrum.
content.english: Ant. Christ our King cometh, Whom John preached, saying: Behold the Lamb That should come!

content.latin: Ant. Ecce vénio * cito et merces mea mecum est, dicit Dóminus: dare unicuíque secúndum ópera sua.
content.english: Ant. Behold, I come * quickly, saith the Lord, and My reward is with Me, to give every man according as his work shall be.

content.latin: 9:12 Psállite Dómino, qui hábitat in Sion: * annuntiáte inter gentes stúdia eius:
content.english: 9:12 Sing ye to the Lord, who dwelleth in Sion: * declare his ways among the Gentiles.

content.latin: 9:13 Quóniam requírens sánguinem eórum recordátus est: * non est oblítus clamórem páuperum.
content.english: 9:13 For requiring their blood he hath remembered them: * he hath not forgotten the cry of the poor.

content.latin: 9:14 Miserére mei, Dómine: * vide humilitátem meam de inimícis meis.
content.english: 9:14 Have mercy on me, O Lord: * see my humiliation which I suffer from my enemies.

content.latin: 9:15 Qui exáltas me de portis mortis, * ut annúntiem omnes laudatiónes tuas in portis fíliæ Sion.
content.english: 9:15 Thou that liftest me up from the gates of death, * that I may declare all thy praises in the gates of the daughter of Sion.

content.latin: 9:16 Exsultábo in salutári tuo: * infíxæ sunt gentes in intéritu, quem fecérunt.
content.english: 9:16 I will rejoice in thy salvation: * the Gentiles have stuck fast in the destruction which they have prepared.

content.latin: 9:16 In láqueo isto, quem abscondérunt, * comprehénsus est pes eórum.
content.english: 9:16 Their foot hath been taken * in the very snare which they hid.

content.latin: 9:17 Cognoscétur Dóminus iudícia fáciens: * in opéribus mánuum suárum comprehénsus est peccátor.
content.english: 9:17 The Lord shall be known when he executeth judgments: * the sinner hath been caught in the works of his own hands.

content.latin: 9:18 Convertántur peccatóres in inférnum, * omnes gentes quæ obliviscúntur Deum.
content.english: 9:18 The wicked shall be turned into hell, * all the nations that forget God.

content.latin: 9:19 Quóniam non in finem oblívio erit páuperis: * patiéntia páuperum non períbit in finem.
content.english: 9:19 For the poor man shall not be forgotten to the end: * the patience of the poor shall not perish for ever.

content.latin: 9:20 Exsúrge, Dómine, non confortétur homo: * iudicéntur gentes in conspéctu tuo.
content.english: 9:20 Arise, O Lord, let not man be strengthened: * let the Gentiles be judged in thy sight.

content.latin: 9:21 Constítue, Dómine, legislatórem super eos: * ut sciant gentes quóniam hómines sunt.
content.english: 9:21 Appoint, O Lord, a lawgiver over them: * that the Gentiles may know themselves to be but men.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Ecce vénio cito et merces mea mecum est, dicit Dóminus: dare unicuíque secúndum ópera sua.
content.english: Ant. Behold, I come quickly, saith the Lord, and My reward is with Me, to give every man according as his work shall be.

content.latin: Ant. Gábriel Ángelus * locútus est Maríæ, dicens: Ave, grátia plena: Dóminus tecum: benedícta tu inter mulíeres.
content.english: Ant. The Angel Gabriel * spake unto Mary, saying: Hail, thou that art full of grace, the Lord is with thee: blessed art thou among women.

content.latin: 9:22 Ut quid, Dómine, recessísti longe, * déspicis in opportunitátibus, in tribulatióne?
content.english: 9:22 Why, O Lord, hast thou retired afar off? * why dost thou slight us in our wants, in the time of trouble?

content.latin: 9:23 Dum supérbit ímpius, incénditur pauper: * comprehendúntur in consíliis quibus cógitant.
content.english: 9:23 Whilst the wicked man is proud, the poor is set on fire: * they are caught in the counsels which they devise.

content.latin: 9:24 Quóniam laudátur peccátor in desidériis ánimæ suæ: * et iníquus benedícitur.
content.english: 9:24 For the sinner is praised in the desires of his soul: * and the unjust man is blessed.

content.latin: 9:25 Exacerbávit Dóminum peccátor, * secúndum multitúdinem iræ suæ non quæret.
content.english: 9:25 The sinner hath provoked the Lord, * according to the multitude of his wrath he will not seek him.

content.latin: 9:26 Non est Deus in conspéctu eius: * inquinátæ sunt viæ illíus in omni témpore.
content.english: 9:26 God is not before his eyes: * his ways are filthy at all times.

content.latin: 9:26 Auferúntur iudícia tua a fácie eius: * ómnium inimicórum suórum dominábitur.
content.english: 9:26 Thy judgments are removed from his sight: * he shall rule over all his enemies.

content.latin: 9:27 Dixit enim in corde suo: * Non movébor a generatióne in generatiónem sine malo.
content.english: 9:27 For he hath said in his heart: * I shall not be moved from generation to generation, and shall be without evil.

content.latin: 9:28 Cuius maledictióne os plenum est, et amaritúdine, et dolo: * sub lingua eius labor et dolor.
content.english: 9:28 His mouth is full of cursing, and of bitterness, and of deceit: * under his tongue are labour and sorrow.

content.latin: 9:29 Sedet in insídiis cum divítibus in occúltis: * ut interfíciat innocéntem.
content.english: 9:29 He sitteth in ambush with the rich, in private places, * that he may kill the innocent.

content.latin: 9:30 Óculi eius in páuperem respíciunt: * insidiátur in abscóndito, quasi leo in spelúnca sua.
content.english: 9:30 His eyes are upon the poor man: * he lieth in wait, in secret, like a lion in his den.

content.latin: 9:30 Insidiátur ut rápiat páuperem: * rápere páuperem, dum áttrahit eum.
content.english: 9:30 He lieth in ambush, that he may catch the poor man: * so catch the poor, whilst he draweth him to him.

content.latin: 9:31 In láqueo suo humiliábit eum: * inclinábit se, et cadet, cum dominátus fúerit páuperum.
content.english: 9:31 In his net he will bring him down, * he will crouch and fall, when he shall have power over the poor.

content.latin: 9:32 Dixit enim in corde suo: Oblítus est Deus, * avértit fáciem suam ne vídeat in finem.
content.english: 9:32 For he hath said in his heart: God hath forgotten, * he hath turned away his face, not to see to the end.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Gábriel Ángelus locútus est Maríæ, dicens: Ave, grátia plena: Dóminus tecum: benedícta tu inter mulíeres.
content.english: Ant. The Angel Gabriel spake unto Mary, saying: Hail, thou that art full of grace, the Lord is with thee: blessed art thou among women.

content.latin: Ant. María dixit: * Putas qualis est ista salutátio, quia conturbáta est ánima mea, et quia paritúra sum Regem, qui claustrum virginitátis meæ non violábit?
content.english: Ant. Mary said: * What manner of salutation is this? My soul is troubled. Shall I bear the King? And will He not break the seal of my virginity?

content.latin: 9:33 Exsúrge, Dómine Deus, exaltétur manus tua: * ne obliviscáris páuperum.
content.english: 9:33 Arise, O Lord God, let thy hand be exalted: * forget not the poor.

content.latin: 9:34 Propter quid irritávit ímpius Deum? * dixit enim in corde suo: Non requíret.
content.english: 9:34 Wherefore hath the wicked provoked God? * for he hath said in his heart: He will not require it.

content.latin: 9:35 Vides quóniam tu labórem et dolórem consíderas: * ut tradas eos in manus tuas.
content.english: 9:35 Thou seest it, for thou considerest labour and sorrow: * that thou mayst deliver them into thy hands.

content.latin: 9:35 Tibi derelíctus est pauper: * órphano tu eris adiútor.
content.english: 9:35 To thee is the poor man left: * thou wilt be a helper to the orphan.

content.latin: 9:36 Cóntere brácchium peccatóris et malígni: * quærétur peccátum illíus, et non inveniétur.
content.english: 9:36 Break thou the arm of the sinner and of the malignant: * his sin shall be sought, and shall not be found.

content.latin: 9:37 Dóminus regnábit in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi: * períbitis, gentes, de terra illíus.
content.english: 9:37 The Lord shall reign to eternity, yea, for ever and ever: * ye Gentiles shall perish from his land.

content.latin: 9:38 Desidérium páuperum exaudívit Dóminus: * præparatiónem cordis eórum audívit auris tua.
content.english: 9:38 The Lord hath heard the desire of the poor: * thy ear hath heard the preparation of their heart.

content.latin: 9:39 Iudicáre pupíllo et húmili, * ut non appónat ultra magnificáre se homo super terram.
content.english: 9:39 To judge for the fatherless and for the humble, * that man may no more presume to magnify himself upon earth.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.english: Ant. Mary said: What manner of salutation is this? My soul is troubled. Shall I bear the King? And will He not break the seal of my virginity?

content.latin: Ant. In advéntu * summi Regis mundéntur corda hóminum, ut digne ambulémus in occúrsum illíus: quia ecce véniet et non tardábit.
content.english: Ant. The King, * even the Most High, cometh therefore let the hearts of men be purified to go forth to meet Him, for, behold, He will come and will not tarry.

content.latin: Psalmus 10 [9]
content.english: Psalm 10 [9]

content.latin: 10:2 In Dómino confído: quómodo dícitis ánimæ meæ: * Tránsmigra in montem sicut passer?
content.english: 10:2 In the Lord I put my trust: how then do you say to my soul: * Get thee away from hence to the mountain, like a sparrow?

content.latin: 10:3 Quóniam ecce peccatóres intendérunt arcum, paravérunt sagíttas suas in pháretra, * ut sagíttent in obscúro rectos corde.
content.english: 10:3 For, lo, the wicked have bent their bow: they have prepared their arrows in the quiver, * to shoot in the dark the upright of heart.

content.latin: 10:4 Quóniam quæ perfecísti, destruxérunt: * iustus autem quid fecit?
content.english: 10:4 For they have destroyed the things which thou hast made: * but what has the just man done?

content.latin: 10:5 Dóminus in templo sancto suo, * Dóminus in cælo sedes eius.
content.english: 10:5 The Lord is in his holy temple, * the Lord’s throne is in heaven.

content.latin: 10:5 Óculi eius in páuperem respíciunt: * pálpebræ eius intérrogant fílios hóminum.
content.english: 10:5 His eyes look on the poor man: * his eyelids examine the sons of men.

content.latin: 10:6 Dóminus intérrogat iustum et ímpium: * qui autem díligit iniquitátem, odit ánimam suam.
content.english: 10:6 The Lord trieth the just and the wicked: * but he that loveth iniquity, hateth his own soul.

content.latin: 10:7 Pluet super peccatóres láqueos: * ignis, et sulphur, et spíritus procellárum pars cálicis eórum.
content.english: 10:7 He shall rain snares upon sinners: * fire and brimstone, and storms of winds, shall be the portion of their cup.

content.latin: 10:8 Quóniam iustus Dóminus, et iustítias diléxit: * æquitátem vidit vultus eius.
content.english: 10:8 For the Lord is just, and hath loved justice: * his countenance hath beheld righteousness.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℣. Ex Sion spécies decóris eius.
content.english: ℣. From Sion, from the place of his greatness.

content.latin: ℟. Deus noster maniféste véniet.
content.english: ℟. Our God shall come manifestly.

content.latin: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: Our Father is said silently until And lead us not into temptation:.

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

content.latin: ℣. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: ℣. And lead us not into temptation:

content.latin: ℟. Sed líbera nos a malo.
content.english: ℟. But deliver us from evil.

content.latin: Absolutio. Exáudi, Dómine Iesu Christe, preces servórum tuórum, et miserére nobis: Qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Absolution. O Lord Jesus Christ, graciously hear the prayers of Thy servants, and have mercy upon us, Who livest and reignest with the Father, and the Holy Ghost, ever world without end.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

content.latin: Benedictio. Ille nos benedícat, qui sine fine vivit et regnat.
content.english: Benediction. May His blessing be upon us who doth live and reign for ever.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: Incipit liber Isaíæ Prophétæ
content.english: Lesson from the book of Isaias

content.latin: 1 Vísio Isaíæ fílii Amos, quam vidit super Iudam et Ierúsalem, in diébus Ozíæ, Ióatham, Achaz, et Ezechíæ, regum Iuda.
content.english: 1 The vision of Isaias the son of Amos, which he saw concerning Juda and Jerusalem in the days of Ozias, Joathan, Achaz, and Ezechias, kings of Juda

content.latin: 2 Audíte, cæli, et áuribus pércipe, terra, quóniam Dóminus locútus est: Fílios enutrívi, et exaltávi: ipsi autem sprevérunt me.
content.english: 2 Hear, O ye heavens, and give ear, O earth, for the Lord hath spoken. I have brought up children, and exalted them: but they have despised me.

content.latin: 3 Cognóvit bos possessórem suum, et ásinus præsépe dómini sui: Israël autem me non cognóvit, et pópulus meus non intelléxit.
content.english: 3 The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his master's crib: but Israel hath not known me, and my people hath not understood.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.latin: ℟. Aspíciens a longe, ecce vídeo Dei poténtiam veniéntem, et nébulam totam terram tegéntem. * Ite óbviam ei, et dícite: * Núntia nobis, si tu es ipse, * Qui regnatúrus es in pópulo Israël.
content.english: ℟. I look from afar, and behold I see the Power of God, coming like as a cloud to cover the land with the hosts of his People: * Go ye out to meet him and say: * Tell us if thou art he, * That shalt reign over God's people Israel.

content.latin: ℣. Quique terrígenæ, et fílii hóminum, simul in unum dives et pauper. Ite óbviam ei, et dícite.
content.english: ℣. All ye that dwell in the world, all ye children of men, high and low, rich and poor, one with another. Go ye out to meet him and say.

content.latin: ℣. Qui regis Israël, inténde, qui dedúcis velut ovem Ioseph. Núntia nobis, si tu es ipse.
content.english: ℣. Hear, O thou Shepherd of Israel, thou that leadest Joseph like a sheep. Tell us if thou art he.

content.latin: ℣. Tóllite portas, príncipes, vestras, et elevámini portæ æternáles, et introíbit Rex glóriæ. Qui regnatúrus es in pópulo Israël.
content.english: ℣. Lift up your heads, O ye gates, and be ye lift up, ye everlasting doors, and the King of Glory shall come in. That shalt reign over God's people Israel.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Aspíciens a longe, ecce vídeo Dei poténtiam veniéntem, et nébulam totam terram tegéntem. * Ite óbviam ei, et dícite: * Núntia nobis, si tu es ipse, * Qui regnatúrus es in pópulo Israël.
content.english: ℟. I look from afar, and behold I see the Power of God, coming like as a cloud to cover the land with the hosts of his People: * Go ye out to meet him and say: * Tell us if thou art he, * That shalt reign over God's people Israel.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

content.latin: Benedictio. Divínum auxílium máneat semper nobíscum.
content.english: Benediction. God's most mighty strength alway be His people's staff and stay.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: 4 Væ genti peccatríci, pópulo gravi iniquitáte, sémini nequam, fíliis scelerátis: dereliquérunt Dóminum, blasphemavérunt Sanctum Israël, abalienáti sunt retrórsum.
content.english: 4 Woe to the sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a wicked seed, ungracious children: they have forsaken the Lord, they have blasphemed the Holy One of Israel, they are gone away backwards.

content.latin: 5 Super quo percútiam vos ultra, addéntes prævaricatiónem? omne caput lánguidum, et omne cor mærens.
content.english: 5 For what shall I strike you any more, you that increase transgression? the whole head is sick, and the whole heart is sad.

content.latin: 6 A planta pedis usque ad vérticem non est in eo sánitas: vulnus, et livor, et plaga tumens non est circumligáta, nec curáta medicámine, neque fota óleo.
content.english: 6 From the sole of the foot unto the top of the head, there is no soundness therein: wounds and bruises and swelling sores: they are not bound up, nor dressed, nor fomented with oil.

content.latin: 7 Terra vestra desérta, civitátes vestræ succénsæ igni: regiónem vestram coram vobis aliéni dévorant, et desolábitur sicut in vastitáte hostíli.
content.english: 7 Your land is desolate, your cities are burnt with fire: your country strangers devour before your face, and it shall be desolate as when wasted by enemies.

content.latin: 8 Et derelinquétur fília Sion ut umbráculum in vínea, et sicut tugúrium in cucumerário, et sicut cívitas quæ vastátur.
content.english: 8 And the daughter of Sion shall be left as a covert in a vineyard, and as a lodge in a garden of cucumbers, and as a city that is laid waste.

content.latin: 9 Nisi Dóminus exercítuum reliquísset nobis semen, quasi Sódoma fuissémus, et quasi Gomórrha símiles essémus.
content.english: 9 Except the Lord of hosts had left us seed, we had been as Sodom, and we should have been like to Gomorrha.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.latin: ℟. Missus est Gábriel Angelus ad Maríam Vírginem desponsátam Ioseph, núntians ei verbum; et expavéscit Virgo de lúmine: ne tímeas, María, invenísti grátiam apud Dóminum:
content.english: ℟. The Angel Gabriel was sent to Mary, a Virgin espoused to Joseph, to bring unto her the word of the Lord, and when the Virgin saw the light, she was afraid. Fear not, Mary, for thou hast found grace from the Lord.

content.latin: * Ecce concípies, et páries, et vocábitur Altíssimi Fílius.
content.english: * Behold, thou shalt conceive and bring forth a son, and He shall be called the Son of the Highest.

content.latin: ℣. Dabit ei Dóminus Deus sedem David, patris eius, et regnábit in domo Iacob in ætérnum.
content.english: ℣. The Lord God shall give unto Him the throne of His father David, and He shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever.

content.latin: ℟. Ecce concípies, et páries, et vocábitur Altíssimi Fílius.
content.english: ℟. Behold, thou shalt conceive, and bring forth a son, and He shall be called the Son of the Highest.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

content.latin: Benedictio. Per evangélica dicta, deleántur nostra delícta.
content.english: Benediction. May the Gospel's glorious word Cleansing to our souls afford.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: Léctio sancti Evangélii secúndum Lucam
content.english: From the Holy Gospel according to Luke

content.latin: In illo témpore: Dixit Iesus discípulis suis: Erunt signa in sole, et luna, et stellis, et in terris pressúra géntium. Et réliqua.
content.english: In that time, Jesus said to his disciples: And there shall be signs in the sun, and in the moon, and in the stars; and upon the earth distress of nations. And so on.

content.latin: Homilía sancti Gregórii Papæ
content.english: Homily by Pope St. Gregory the Great,

content.latin: Homilia 1 in Evangelia
content.english: 1st on the Gospels

content.latin: Dóminus ac Redémptor noster parátos nos inveníre desíderans, senescéntem mundum quæ mala sequántur denúntiat, ut nos ab eius amóre compéscat. Appropinquántem eius términum quantæ percussiónes prævéniant, innotéscit: ut, si Deum metúere in tranquillitáte nólumus, saltem vicínum eius iudícium vel percussiónibus attríti timeámus.
content.english: Our Lord and Saviour wisheth to find us ready at His second coming. Therefore He telleth us what will be the evils of the world as it groweth old, that He may wean our hearts from worldly affections. Here we read what great convulsions will go before the end, that, if we will not fear God in our prosperity, we may at least be scourged into fearing His judgment when it is at hand.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.latin: ℟. Ecce dies véniunt, dicit Dóminus, et suscitábo David germen iustum: et regnábit rex, et sápiens erit, et fáciet iudícium et iustítiam in terra:
content.english: ℟. Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch; and a King shall reign in wisdom and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth:

content.latin: * Et hoc est nomen quod vocábunt eum: * Dóminus iustus noster.
content.english: * And this is His name whereby He shall be called: * The Lord our Righteous one.

content.latin: ℣. In diébus illis salvábitur Iuda, et Israël habitábit confidénter.
content.english: ℣. In His days Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell safely.

content.latin: ℟. Et hoc est nomen quod vocábunt eum:
content.english: ℟. And this is His name whereby He shall be called.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Dóminus iustus noster.
content.english: ℟. The Lord our Righteous one.

content.latin: Reliqua omittuntur, nisi separandæ sint.
content.english: Skip the rest, unless praying separately.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Excita, quǽsumus, Dómine, poténtiam tuam, et veni: ut ab imminéntibus peccatórum nostrórum perículis, te mereámur protegénte éripi, te liberánte salvári:
content.english: Stir up, O Lord, we pray thee, thy strength, and come among us, that whereas through our sins and wickedness we do justly apprehend thy wrathful judgments hanging over us, thy bountiful grace and mercy may speedily help and deliver us;

content.latin: Qui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre, in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Who livest and reignest with God the Father in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, world without end.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

content.latin: ℣. Benedicámus Dómino.
content.english: ℣. Let us bless the Lord.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.latin: ℣. Fidélium ánimæ per misericórdiam Dei requiéscant in pace.
content.english: ℣. May the souls of the faithful, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Deus ✠ in adiutórium meum inténde.
content.english: ℣. O God, ✠ come to my assistance;

content.latin: ℟. Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.
content.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.

content.latin: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Allelúia.
content.english: Alleluia.

content.latin: Ant. In illa die * stillábunt montes dulcédinem, et colles fluent lac et mel, allelúia.
content.english: Ant. In that day * the mountains shall drop down sweet wine, and the hills shall flow with milk and honey. Alleluia.

content.latin: Psalmus 92 [1]
content.english: Psalm 92 [1]

content.latin: 92:1 Dóminus regnávit, decórem indútus est: * indútus est Dóminus fortitúdinem, et præcínxit se.
content.english: 92:1 The Lord hath reigned, he is clothed with beauty: * the Lord is clothed with strength, and hath girded himself.

content.latin: 92:1 Étenim firmávit orbem terræ, * qui non commovébitur.
content.english: 92:1 For he hath established the world * which shall not be moved.

content.latin: 92:2 Paráta sedes tua ex tunc: * a sǽculo tu es.
content.english: 92:2 Thy throne is prepared from of old: * thou art from everlasting.

content.latin: 92:3 Elevavérunt flúmina, Dómine: * elevavérunt flúmina vocem suam.
content.english: 92:3 The floods have lifted up, O Lord: * the floods have lifted up their voice.

content.latin: 92:3 Elevavérunt flúmina fluctus suos, * a vócibus aquárum multárum.
content.english: 92:3 The floods have lifted up their waves, * with the noise of many waters.

content.latin: 92:4 Mirábiles elatiónes maris: * mirábilis in altis Dóminus.
content.english: 92:4 Wonderful are the surges of the sea: * wonderful is the Lord on high.

content.latin: 92:5 Testimónia tua credibília facta sunt nimis: * domum tuam decet sanctitúdo, Dómine, in longitúdinem diérum.
content.english: 92:5 Thy testimonies are become exceedingly credible: * holiness becometh thy house, O Lord, unto length of days.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. In illa die stillábunt montes dulcédinem, et colles fluent lac et mel, allelúia.
content.english: Ant. In that day the mountains shall drop down sweet wine, and the hills shall flow with milk and honey. Alleluia.

content.latin: Ant. Iucundáre, * fília Sion, et exsúlta satis, fília Ierúsalem, allelúia.
content.english: Ant. Sing, O daughter of Zion, * and rejoice with all the heart, O daughter of Jerusalem. Alleluia.

content.latin: Psalmus 99 [2]
content.english: Psalm 99 [2]

content.latin: 99:2 Iubiláte Deo, omnis terra: * servíte Dómino in lætítia.
content.english: 99:2 Sing joyfully to God, all the earth: * serve ye the Lord with gladness.

content.latin: 99:2 Introíte in conspéctu eius, * in exsultatióne.
content.english: 99:2 Come in before his presence * with exceeding great joy.

content.latin: 99:3 Scitóte quóniam Dóminus ipse est Deus: * ipse fecit nos, et non ipsi nos.
content.english: 99:3 Know ye that the Lord he is God: * he made us, and not we ourselves.

content.latin: 99:3 Pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius: * introíte portas eius in confessióne, átria eius in hymnis: confitémini illi.
content.english: 99:3 We are his people and the sheep of his pasture. * Go ye into his gates with praise, into his courts with hymns: and give glory to him.

content.latin: 99:4 Laudáte nomen eius: quóniam suávis est Dóminus, in ætérnum misericórdia eius, * et usque in generatiónem et generatiónem véritas eius.
content.english: 99:4 Praise ye his name: for the Lord is sweet, his mercy endureth for ever, * and his truth to generation and generation.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Iucundáre, fília Sion, et exsúlta satis, fília Ierúsalem, allelúia.
content.english: Ant. Sing, O daughter of Zion, and rejoice with all the heart, O daughter of Jerusalem. Alleluia.

content.latin: Ant. Ecce Dóminus véniet, * et omnes Sancti eius cum eo: et erit in die illa lux magna, allelúia.
content.english: Ant. Behold, the Lord shall come, * and all His saints with Him; and it shall come to pass in that day that the light shall be great. Alleluia.

content.latin: Psalmus 62 [3]
content.english: Psalm 62 [3]

content.latin: 62:2 Deus, Deus meus, * ad te de luce vígilo.
content.english: 62:2 O God, my God, * to thee do I watch at break of day.

content.latin: 62:2 Sitívit in te ánima mea, * quam multiplíciter tibi caro mea.
content.english: 62:2 For thee my soul hath thirsted; * for thee my flesh, O how many ways!

content.latin: 62:3 In terra desérta, et ínvia, et inaquósa: * sic in sancto appárui tibi, ut vidérem virtútem tuam, et glóriam tuam.
content.english: 62:3 In a desert land, and where there is no way, and no water: * so in the sanctuary have I come before thee, to see thy power and thy glory.

content.latin: 62:4 Quóniam mélior est misericórdia tua super vitas: * lábia mea laudábunt te.
content.english: 62:4 For thy mercy is better than lives: * thee my lips shall praise.

content.latin: 62:5 Sic benedícam te in vita mea: * et in nómine tuo levábo manus meas.
content.english: 62:5 Thus will I bless thee all my life long: * and in thy name I will lift up my hands.

content.latin: 62:6 Sicut ádipe et pinguédine repleátur ánima mea: * et lábiis exsultatiónis laudábit os meum.
content.english: 62:6 Let my soul be filled as with marrow and fatness: * and my mouth shall praise thee with joyful lips.

content.latin: 62:7 Si memor fui tui super stratum meum, in matutínis meditábor in te: * quia fuísti adiútor meus.
content.english: 62:7 If I have remembered thee upon my bed, I will meditate on thee in the morning: * because thou hast been my helper.

content.latin: 62:8 Et in velaménto alárum tuárum exsultábo, adhǽsit ánima mea post te: * me suscépit déxtera tua.
content.english: 62:8 And I will rejoice under the covert of thy wings: my soul hath stuck close to thee: * thy right hand hath received me.

content.latin: 62:10 Ipsi vero in vanum quæsiérunt ánimam meam, introíbunt in inferióra terræ: * tradéntur in manus gládii, partes vúlpium erunt.
content.english: 62:10 But they have sought my soul in vain, they shall go into the lower parts of the earth: * they shall be delivered into the hands of the sword, they shall be the portions of foxes.

content.latin: 62:12 Rex vero lætábitur in Deo, laudabúntur omnes qui iurant in eo: * quia obstrúctum est os loquéntium iníqua.
content.english: 62:12 But the king shall rejoice in God, all they shall be praised that swear by him: * because the mouth is stopped of them that speak wicked things.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Canticum Trium Puerorum [4]
content.english: Canticle of the Three Young Men [4]

content.latin: 3:57 Benedícite, ómnia ópera Dómini, Dómino: * laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:57 All ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord: * praise and exalt him above all for ever.

content.latin: 3:58 Benedícite, Ángeli Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, cæli, Dómino.
content.english: 3:58 O ye angels of the Lord, bless the Lord: * O ye heavens, bless the Lord:

content.latin: 3:59 Benedícite, aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes virtútes Dómini, Dómino.
content.english: 3:59 O all ye waters that are above the heavens, bless the Lord: * O all ye powers of the Lord, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 3:60 Benedícite, sol et luna, Dómino: * benedícite, stellæ cæli, Dómino.
content.english: 3:60 O ye sun and moon, bless the Lord: * O ye stars of heaven, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 3:61 Benedícite, omnis imber et ros, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes spíritus Dei, Dómino.
content.english: 3:61 O every shower and dew, bless ye the Lord: * O all ye spirits of God, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 3:62 Benedícite, ignis et æstus, Dómino: * benedícite, frigus et æstus, Dómino.
content.english: 3:62 O ye fire and heat, bless the Lord: * O ye cold and heat, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 3:63 Benedícite, rores et pruína, Dómino: * benedícite, gelu et frigus, Dómino.
content.english: 3:63 O ye dews and hoar frosts, bless the Lord: * O ye frost and cold, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 3:64 Benedícite, glácies et nives, Dómino: * benedícite, noctes et dies, Dómino.
content.english: 3:64 O ye ice and snow, bless the Lord: * O ye nights and days, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 3:65 Benedícite, lux et ténebræ, Dómino: * benedícite, fúlgura et nubes, Dómino.
content.english: 3:65 O ye light and darkness, bless the Lord: * O ye lightnings and clouds, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 3:66 Benedícat terra Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:66 O let the earth bless the Lord: * let it praise and exalt him above all for ever.

content.latin: 3:67 Benedícite, montes et colles, Dómino: * benedícite, univérsa germinántia in terra, Dómino.
content.english: 3:67 O ye mountains and hills, bless the Lord: * O all ye things that spring up in the earth, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 3:68 Benedícite, fontes, Dómino: * benedícite, mária et flúmina, Dómino.
content.english: 3:68 O ye fountains, bless the Lord: * O ye seas and rivers, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 3:69 Benedícite, cete, et ómnia, quæ movéntur in aquis, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes vólucres cæli, Dómino.
content.english: 3:69 O ye whales, and all that move in the waters, bless the Lord: * O all ye fowls of the air, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 3:70 Benedícite, omnes béstiæ et pécora, Dómino: * benedícite, fílii hóminum, Dómino.
content.english: 3:70 O all ye beasts and cattle, bless the Lord: * O ye sons of men, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 3:71 Benedícat Israël Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:71 O let Israel bless the Lord: * let them praise and exalt him above all for ever.

content.latin: 3:72 Benedícite, sacerdótes Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, servi Dómini, Dómino.
content.english: 3:72 O ye priests of the Lord, bless the Lord: * O ye servants of the Lord, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 3:73 Benedícite, spíritus, et ánimæ iustórum, Dómino: * benedícite, sancti, et húmiles corde, Dómino.
content.english: 3:73 O ye spirits and souls of the just, bless the Lord: * O ye holy and humble of heart, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 3:74 Benedícite, Ananía, Azaría, Mísaël, Dómino: * laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:74 O Ananias, Azarias, and Misael, bless ye the Lord: * praise and exalt him above all for ever.

content.latin: 3:75 (Fit reverentia:) Benedicámus Patrem et Fílium cum Sancto Spíritu: * laudémus et superexaltémus eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:75 (Bow head) Let us bless the Father and the Son, with the Holy Ghost; * let us praise and exalt him above all for ever.

content.latin: 3:56 Benedíctus es, Dómine, in firmaménto cæli: * et laudábilis, et gloriósus, et superexaltátus in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:56 Blessed art thou, O Lord, in the firmament of heaven: * and worthy of praise, and glorious for ever.

content.latin: Ant. Omnes sitiéntes, veníte ad aquas: quǽrite Dóminum, dum inveníri potest, allelúia.
content.english: Ant. Lo, every one that thirsteth come ye to the waters: seek ye the Lord while He may be found. Alleluia.

content.latin: Ant. Ecce véniet * Prophéta magnus, et ipse renovábit Ierúsalem, allelúia.
content.english: Ant. Behold, a great Prophet * shall arise, and He shall build up a new Jerusalem. Alleluia.

content.latin: Psalmus 148 [5]
content.english: Psalm 148 [5]

content.latin: 148:1 Laudáte Dóminum de cælis: * laudáte eum in excélsis.
content.english: 148:1 Praise ye the Lord from the heavens * praise ye him in the high places.

content.latin: 148:2 Laudáte eum, omnes Ángeli eius: * laudáte eum, omnes virtútes eius.
content.english: 148:2 Praise ye him, all his angels: * praise ye him, all his hosts.

content.latin: 148:3 Laudáte eum, sol et luna: * laudáte eum, omnes stellæ et lumen.
content.english: 148:3 Praise ye him, O sun and moon: * praise him, all ye stars and light.

content.latin: 148:4 Laudáte eum, cæli cælórum: * et aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, laudent nomen Dómini.
content.english: 148:4 Praise him, ye heavens of heavens: * and let all the waters that are above the heavens, praise the name of the Lord.

content.latin: 148:5 Quia ipse dixit, et facta sunt: * ipse mandávit, et creáta sunt.
content.english: 148:5 For he spoke, and they were made: * he commanded, and they were created.

content.latin: 148:6 Státuit ea in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi: * præcéptum pósuit, et non præteríbit.
content.english: 148:6 He hath established them for ever, and for ages of ages: * he hath made a decree, and it shall not pass away.

content.latin: 148:7 Laudáte Dóminum de terra, * dracónes, et omnes abýssi.
content.english: 148:7 Praise the Lord from the earth, * ye dragons, and all ye deeps:

content.latin: 148:8 Ignis, grando, nix, glácies, spíritus procellárum: * quæ fáciunt verbum eius:
content.english: 148:8 Fire, hail, snow, ice, stormy winds * which fulfill his word:

content.latin: 148:9 Montes, et omnes colles: * ligna fructífera, et omnes cedri.
content.english: 148:9 Mountains and all hills, * fruitful trees and all cedars:

content.latin: 148:10 Béstiæ, et univérsa pécora: * serpéntes, et vólucres pennátæ:
content.english: 148:10 Beasts and all cattle: * serpents and feathered fowls:

content.latin: 148:11 Reges terræ, et omnes pópuli: * príncipes, et omnes iúdices terræ.
content.english: 148:11 Kings of the earth and all people: * princes and all judges of the earth:

content.latin: 148:12 Iúvenes, et vírgines: senes cum iunióribus laudent nomen Dómini: * quia exaltátum est nomen eius solíus.
content.english: 148:12 Young men and maidens: let the old with the younger, praise the name of the Lord: * For his name alone is exalted.

content.latin: 148:14 Conféssio eius super cælum et terram: * et exaltávit cornu pópuli sui.
content.english: 148:14 The praise of him is above heaven and earth: * and he hath exalted the horn of his people.

content.latin: 148:14 Hymnus ómnibus sanctis eius: * fíliis Israël, pópulo appropinquánti sibi.
content.english: 148:14 A hymn to all his saints: to the children of Israel, a people approaching him.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Ecce véniet Prophéta magnus, et ipse renovábit Ierúsalem, allelúia.
content.english: Ant. Behold, a great Prophet shall arise, and He shall build up a new Jerusalem. Alleluia.

content.latin: Fratres: Hora est iam nos de somno súrgere: nunc enim própior est nostra salus, quam cum credídimus.
content.english: And that knowing the season; that it is now the hour for us to rise from sleep. For now our salvation is nearer than when we believed.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.latin: Hymnus
content.english: Hymn

content.latin: En clara vox redárguit
content.english: Hark, a herald voice is calling;

content.latin: Obscúra quæque, pérsonans:
content.english: “Christ is nigh,” it seems to say;

content.latin: Procul fugéntur sómnia,
content.english: “Cast away the dreams of darkness,

content.latin: Ab alto Iesus prómicat.
content.english: O ye children of the day.”

content.latin: Mens iam resúrgat, tórpida,
content.english: Startled at the solemn warning,

content.latin: Non ámplius iacens humi:
content.english: Let the earth-bound soul arise;

content.latin: Sidus refúlget iam novum,
content.english: Christ, her sun, all sloth dispelling,

content.latin: Ut tollat omne nóxium.
content.english: Shines upon the morning skies.

content.latin: En Agnus ad nos míttitur
content.english: Lo, the Lamb, so long expected,

content.latin: Laxáre gratis débitum:
content.english: Comes with pardon down from heaven;

content.latin: Omnes simul cum lácrimis
content.english: Let us haste, with tears of sorrow,

content.latin: Precémur indulgéntiam.
content.english: One and all to be forgiven.

content.latin: Ut cum secúndo fúlserit,
content.english: So when next he comes with glory,

content.latin: Metúque mundum cínxerit,
content.english: Wrapping all the earth in fear,

content.latin: Non pro reátu púniat,
content.english: May he then as our defender

content.latin: Sed nos pius tunc prótegat.
content.english: On the clouds of heaven appear.

content.latin: Virtus, honor, laus, glória
content.english: Honour, glory, virtue, merit,

content.latin: Deo Patri cum Fílio,
content.english: To the Father and the Son,

content.latin: Sancto simul Paráclito,
content.english: With the co-eternal Spirit,

content.latin: In sæculórum sǽcula.
content.english: While eternal ages run.

content.latin: Amen.
content.english: Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Vox clamántis in desérto: Paráte viam Dómini.
content.english: ℣. A voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord.

content.latin: ℟. Rectas fácite sémitas eius.
content.english: ℟. Make straight his paths.

content.latin: Ant. Spíritus Sanctus * in te descéndet, María: ne tímeas, habébis in útero Fílium Dei, allelúia.
content.english: Ant. The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, * O Mary; fear not, thou shalt bear in thy womb the Son of God. Alleluia.

content.latin: Canticum Zachariæ
content.english: Canticle of Zacharias

content.latin: 1:68 Benedíctus ✠ Dóminus, Deus Israël: * quia visitávit, et fecit redemptiónem plebis suæ:
content.english: 1:68 Blessed be the Lord ✠ God of Israel; * because he hath visited and wrought the redemption of his people:

content.latin: 1:69 Et eréxit cornu salútis nobis: * in domo David, púeri sui.
content.english: 1:69 And hath raised up an horn of salvation to us, * in the house of David his servant:

content.latin: 1:70 Sicut locútus est per os sanctórum, * qui a sǽculo sunt, prophetárum eius:
content.english: 1:70 As he spoke by the mouth of his holy Prophets, * who are from the beginning:

content.latin: 1:71 Salútem ex inimícis nostris, * et de manu ómnium, qui odérunt nos.
content.english: 1:71 Salvation from our enemies, * and from the hand of all that hate us:

content.latin: 1:72 Ad faciéndam misericórdiam cum pátribus nostris: * et memorári testaménti sui sancti.
content.english: 1:72 To perform mercy to our fathers, * and to remember his holy testament,

content.latin: 1:73 Iusiurándum, quod iurávit ad Ábraham patrem nostrum, * datúrum se nobis:
content.english: 1:73 The oath, which he swore to Abraham our father, * that he would grant to us,

content.latin: 1:74 Ut sine timóre, de manu inimicórum nostrórum liberáti, * serviámus illi.
content.english: 1:74 That being delivered from the hand of our enemies, * we may serve him without fear,

content.latin: 1:75 In sanctitáte, et iustítia coram ipso, * ómnibus diébus nostris.
content.english: 1:75 In holiness and justice before him, * all our days.

content.latin: 1:76 Et tu, puer, Prophéta Altíssimi vocáberis: * præíbis enim ante fáciem Dómini, paráre vias eius:
content.english: 1:76 And thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest: * for thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways:

content.latin: 1:77 Ad dandam sciéntiam salútis plebi eius: * in remissiónem peccatórum eórum:
content.english: 1:77 To give knowledge of salvation to his people, * unto the remission of their sins:

content.latin: 1:78 Per víscera misericórdiæ Dei nostri: * in quibus visitávit nos, óriens ex alto:
content.english: 1:78 Through the bowels of the mercy of our God, * in which the Orient from on high hath visited us:

content.latin: 1:79 Illumináre his, qui in ténebris, et in umbra mortis sedent: * ad dirigéndos pedes nostros in viam pacis.
content.english: 1:79 To enlighten them that sit in darkness, and in the shadow of death: * to direct our feet into the way of peace.

content.english: Ant. Zacchaeus, make haste and come down, for today I must abide at thy house. And he made haste and came down, and received Him joyfully into his house. This day is salvation come from God to this house. Alleluia.

content.english: Prayer on the anniversary of the dedication:

content.latin: Deus, qui nobis per síngulos annos huius sancti templi tui consecratiónis réparas diem, et sacris semper mystériis repræséntas incólumes: exáudi preces pópuli tui, et præsta; ut quisquis hoc templum benefícia petitúrus ingréditur, cuncta se impetrásse lætétur.
content.english: O God, who dost every year bring round unto us again the day whereon this thine holy temple was hallowed, and bringest us again in soundness of body and mind to be present at thine holy worship, graciously hear the supplications of thy people, and grant that whosoever shall come into this thine house to ask good at thine hand, may be rejoiced in the obtaining of all his request.

content.latin: Per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.

content.english: Now in the sun's new dawning ray,

content.latin: 117:1 Confitémini Dómino quóniam bonus: * quóniam in sǽculum misericórdia eius.
content.english: 117:1 Give praise to the Lord, for he is good: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

content.latin: 117:2 Dicat nunc Israël quóniam bonus: * quóniam in sǽculum misericórdia eius.
content.english: 117:2 Let Israel now say, that he is good: * that his mercy endureth for ever.

content.latin: 117:3 Dicat nunc domus Aaron: * quóniam in sǽculum misericórdia eius.
content.english: 117:3 Let the house of Aaron now say, * that his mercy endureth for ever.

content.latin: 117:4 Dicant nunc qui timent Dóminum: * quóniam in sǽculum misericórdia eius.
content.english: 117:4 Let them that fear the Lord now say, * that his mercy endureth for ever.

content.latin: 117:5 De tribulatióne invocávi Dóminum: * et exaudívit me in latitúdine Dóminus.
content.english: 117:5 In my trouble I called upon the Lord: * and the Lord heard me, and enlarged me.

content.latin: 117:6 Dóminus mihi adiútor: * non timébo quid fáciat mihi homo.
content.english: 117:6 The Lord is my helper: * I will not fear what man can do unto me.

content.latin: 117:7 Dóminus mihi adiútor: * et ego despíciam inimícos meos.
content.english: 117:7 The Lord is my helper: * and I will look over my enemies.

content.latin: 117:8 Bonum est confídere in Dómino, * quam confídere in hómine:
content.english: 117:8 It is good to confide in the Lord, * rather than to have confidence in man.

content.latin: 117:9 Bonum est speráre in Dómino, * quam speráre in princípibus.
content.english: 117:9 It is good to trust in the Lord, * rather than to trust in princes.

content.latin: 117:10 Omnes gentes circuiérunt me: * et in nómine Dómini quia ultus sum in eos.
content.english: 117:10 All nations compassed me about; * and in the name of the Lord I have been revenged on them.

content.latin: 117:11 Circumdántes circumdedérunt me: * et in nómine Dómini quia ultus sum in eos.
content.english: 117:11 Surrounding me they compassed me about: * and in the name of the Lord I have been revenged on them.

content.latin: 117:12 Circumdedérunt me sicut apes, et exarsérunt sicut ignis in spinis: * et in nómine Dómini quia ultus sum in eos.
content.english: 117:12 They surrounded me like bees, and they burned like fire among thorns: * and in the name of the Lord I was revenged on them.

content.latin: 117:13 Impúlsus evérsus sum ut cáderem: * et Dóminus suscépit me.
content.english: 117:13 Being pushed I was overturned that I might fall: * but the Lord supported me.

content.latin: 117:14 Fortitúdo mea, et laus mea Dóminus: * et factus est mihi in salútem.
content.english: 117:14 The Lord is my strength and my praise: * and he is become my salvation.

content.latin: 117:15 Vox exsultatiónis, et salútis * in tabernáculis iustórum.
content.english: 117:15 The voice of rejoicing and of salvation * is in the tabernacles of the just.

content.latin: 117:16 Déxtera Dómini fecit virtútem: déxtera Dómini exaltávit me, * déxtera Dómini fecit virtútem.
content.english: 117:16 The right hand of the Lord hath wrought strength: the right hand of the Lord hath exalted me: * the right hand of the Lord hath wrought strength.

content.latin: 117:17 Non móriar, sed vivam: * et narrábo ópera Dómini.
content.english: 117:17 I shall not die, but live: * and shall declare the works of the Lord.

content.latin: 117:18 Castígans castigávit me Dóminus: * et morti non trádidit me.
content.english: 117:18 The Lord chastising hath chastised me: * but he hath not delivered me over to death.

content.latin: 117:19 Aperíte mihi portas iustítiæ, ingréssus in eas confitébor Dómino: * hæc porta Dómini, iusti intrábunt in eam.
content.english: 117:19 Open ye to me the gates of justice: I will go in to them, and give praise to the Lord. * This is the gate of the Lord, the just shall enter into it.

content.latin: 117:21 Confitébor tibi quóniam exaudísti me: * et factus es mihi in salútem.
content.english: 117:21 I will give glory to thee because thou hast heard me: * and art become my salvation.

content.latin: 117:22 Lápidem, quem reprobavérunt ædificántes: * hic factus est in caput ánguli.
content.english: 117:22 The stone which the builders rejected; * the same is become the head of the corner.

content.latin: 117:23 A Dómino factum est istud: * et est mirábile in óculis nostris.
content.english: 117:23 This is the Lord’s doing: * and it is wonderful in our eyes.

content.latin: 117:24 Hæc est dies, quam fecit Dóminus: * exsultémus, et lætémur in ea.
content.english: 117:24 This is the day which the Lord hath made: * let us be glad and rejoice therein.

content.latin: 117:25 O Dómine, salvum me fac, o Dómine, bene prosperáre: * benedíctus qui venit in nómine Dómini.
content.english: 117:25 O Lord, save me: O Lord, give good success: * Blessed be he that cometh in the name of the Lord.

content.latin: 117:26 Benedíximus vobis de domo Dómini: * Deus Dóminus, et illúxit nobis.
content.english: 117:26 We have blessed you out of the house of the Lord: * The Lord is God, and he hath shone upon us.

content.latin: 117:27 Constitúite diem solémnem in condénsis, * usque ad cornu altáris.
content.english: 117:27 Appoint a solemn day, with shady boughs, * even to the horn of the altar.

content.latin: 117:28 Deus meus es tu, et confitébor tibi: * Deus meus es tu, et exaltábo te.
content.english: 117:28 Thou art my God, and I will praise thee: * thou art my God, and I will exalt thee.

content.latin: 117:28 Confitébor tibi quóniam exaudísti me * et factus es mihi in salútem.
content.english: 117:28 I will praise thee, because thou hast heard me, * and art become my salvation.

content.latin: 117:29 Confitémini Dómino quóniam bonus: * quóniam in sǽculum misericórdia eius.
content.english: 117:29 O praise ye the Lord, for he is good: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

content.latin: 118:1 (Aleph) Beáti immaculáti in via: * qui ámbulant in lege Dómini.
content.english: 118:1 (Aleph) Blessed are the undefiled in the way, * who walk in the law of the Lord.

content.latin: 118:2 Beáti, qui scrutántur testimónia eius: * in toto corde exquírunt eum.
content.english: 118:2 Blessed are they that search his testimonies: * that seek him with their whole heart.

content.latin: 118:3 Non enim qui operántur iniquitátem, * in viis eius ambulavérunt.
content.english: 118:3 For they that work iniquity, * have not walked in his ways.

content.latin: 118:4 Tu mandásti * mandáta tua custodíri nimis.
content.english: 118:4 Thou hast commanded * thy commandments to be kept most diligently.

content.latin: 118:5 Útinam dirigántur viæ meæ, * ad custodiéndas iustificatiónes tuas!
content.english: 118:5 O! that my ways may be directed * to keep thy justifications.

content.latin: 118:6 Tunc non confúndar, * cum perspéxero in ómnibus mandátis tuis.
content.english: 118:6 Then shall I not be confounded, * when I shall look into all thy commandments.

content.latin: 118:7 Confitébor tibi in directióne cordis: * in eo quod dídici iudícia iustítiæ tuæ.
content.english: 118:7 I will praise thee with uprightness of heart, * when I shall have learned the judgments of thy justice.

content.latin: 118:8 Iustificatiónes tuas custódiam: * non me derelínquas usquequáque.
content.english: 118:8 I will keep thy justifications: * O! do not thou utterly forsake me.

content.latin: 118:9 (Beth) In quo córrigit adolescéntior viam suam? * In custodiéndo sermónes tuos.
content.english: 118:9 (Béth) By what doth a young man correct his way? * By observing thy words.

content.latin: 118:10 In toto corde meo exquisívi te: * ne repéllas me a mandátis tuis.
content.english: 118:10 With my whole heart have I sought after thee: * let me not stray from thy commandments.

content.latin: 118:11 In corde meo abscóndi elóquia tua: * ut non peccem tibi.
content.english: 118:11 Thy words have I hidden in my heart, * that I may not sin against thee.

content.latin: 118:12 Benedíctus es, Dómine: * doce me iustificatiónes tuas.
content.english: 118:12 Blessed art thou, O Lord: * teach me thy justifications.

content.latin: 118:13 In lábiis meis, * pronuntiávi ómnia iudícia oris tui.
content.english: 118:13 With my lips * I have pronounced all the judgments of thy mouth.

content.latin: 118:14 In via testimoniórum tuórum delectátus sum, * sicut in ómnibus divítiis.
content.english: 118:14 I have been delighted in the way of thy testimonies, * as in all riches.

content.latin: 118:15 In mandátis tuis exercébor: * et considerábo vias tuas.
content.english: 118:15 I will meditate on thy commandments: * and I will consider thy ways.

content.latin: 118:16 In iustificatiónibus tuis meditábor: * non oblivíscar sermónes tuos.
content.english: 118:16 I will think of thy justifications: * I will not forget thy words.

content.latin: 118:17 (Ghimel) Retríbue servo tuo, vivífica me: * et custódiam sermónes tuos:
content.english: 118:17 (Ghimel) Give bountifully to thy servant, enliven me * and I shall keep thy words.

content.latin: 118:18 Revéla óculos meos: * et considerábo mirabília de lege tua.
content.english: 118:18 Open thou my eyes: * and I will consider the wondrous things of thy law.

content.latin: 118:19 Íncola ego sum in terra: * non abscóndas a me mandáta tua.
content.english: 118:19 I am a sojourner on the earth: * hide not thy commandments from me.

content.latin: 118:20 Concupívit ánima mea desideráre iustificatiónes tuas, * in omni témpore.
content.english: 118:20 My soul hath coveted to long for thy justifications, * at all times.

content.latin: 118:21 Increpásti supérbos: * maledícti qui declínant a mandátis tuis.
content.english: 118:21 Thou hast rebuked the proud: * they are cursed who decline from thy commandments.

content.latin: 118:22 Aufer a me oppróbrium, et contémptum: * quia testimónia tua exquisívi.
content.english: 118:22 Remove from me reproach and contempt: * because I have sought after thy testimonies.

content.latin: 118:23 Étenim sedérunt príncipes, et advérsum me loquebántur: * servus autem tuus exercebátur in iustificatiónibus tuis.
content.english: 118:23 For princes sat, and spoke against me: * but thy servant was employed in thy justifications.

content.latin: 118:24 Nam et testimónia tua meditátio mea est: * et consílium meum iustificatiónes tuæ.
content.english: 118:24 For thy testimonies are my meditation: * and thy justifications my counsel.

content.latin: 118:25 (Daleth) Adhǽsit paviménto ánima mea: * vivífica me secúndum verbum tuum.
content.english: 118:25 (Daleth) My soul hath cleaved to the pavement: * quicken thou me according to thy word.

content.latin: 118:26 Vias meas enuntiávi, et exaudísti me: * doce me iustificatiónes tuas.
content.english: 118:26 I have declared my ways, and thou hast heard me: * teach me thy justifications.

content.latin: 118:27 Viam iustificatiónum tuárum ínstrue me: * et exercébor in mirabílibus tuis.
content.english: 118:27 Make me to understand the way of thy justifications: * and I shall be exercised in thy wondrous works.

content.latin: 118:28 Dormitávit ánima mea præ tǽdio: * confírma me in verbis tuis.
content.english: 118:28 My soul hath slumbered through heaviness: * strengthen thou me in thy words.

content.latin: 118:29 Viam iniquitátis ámove a me: * et de lege tua miserére mei.
content.english: 118:29 Remove from me the way of iniquity: * and out of thy law have mercy on me.

content.latin: 118:30 Viam veritátis elégi: * iudícia tua non sum oblítus.
content.english: 118:30 I have chosen the way of truth: * thy judgments I have not forgotten.

content.latin: 118:31 Adhǽsi testimóniis tuis, Dómine: * noli me confúndere.
content.english: 118:31 I have stuck to thy testimonies, O Lord: * put me not to shame.

content.latin: 118:32 Viam mandatórum tuórum cucúrri, * cum dilatásti cor meum.
content.english: 118:32 I have run the way of thy commandments, * when thou didst enlarge my heart.

content.english: O Lord, our heavenly Father, Almighty and everlasting God, who has safely brought us to the beginning of this day: defend us by thy mighty power; and grant that this day we fall into no sin, but that all our doings may be ordered by thy governance, to do always what is righteous in thy sight.

content.latin: Apud Patras, in Acháia, natális sancti Andréæ Apóstoli, qui in Thrácia et Scýthia sacrum Christi Evangélium prædicávit. Is, ab Ægéa Procónsule comprehénsus, primum in cárcere clausus est, deínde gravíssime cæsus, ad últimum suspénsus in cruce, in ea pópulum docens bíduo supervíxit; et, rogáto Dómino ne eum síneret de cruce depóni, circúmdatus est magno splendóre de cælo, et, abscedénte póstmodum lúmine, emísit spíritum.
content.english: At Patrae, in the Peloponnesus, the holy Apostle Andrew. He preached the Gospel of Christ in Thrace and Scythia. He was arrested by the Proconsul Aegeas, and first imprisoned, then heavily flogged, and, lastly, crucified. He remained alive upon the cross through the second day, and taught the people. He besought the Lord not to suffer him to be taken down from the cross, and then a great light from heaven shone round about him, and when it faded away he gave up the ghost.

content.latin: Romæ pássio sanctórum Cástuli et Euprépitis.

content.english: At Saintes, (in the sixth century,) holy Trojan, Bishop (of that see,) a man of great holiness, who, albeit he be buried in the earth, yet showeth by many works of power that he is alive in heaven.

content.latin: Apud Sántonas, in Gállia, sancti Troiáni Epíscopi, magnæ sanctitátis viri, qui, sepúltus in terris, se in cælis vívere multis virtútibus maniféstat.
content.english: At Rome, (in the fifth century,) the holy Confessor Constantius, who manfully withstood the Pelagians, and bore much at their hands, the which contendings have gained him a place among the holy Confessors.
